The folder `data/` holds the data behind a published data story, "You Know Karen": https://pudding.cool/2020/06/karen/
The files: data/byYear.csv

Write down the story's findings that this data reproduces.

1. Read the story on the web. web_fetch returns the page as the server sends it. web_view opens it in a browser and scrolls it like a reader, so it also gets text drawn by scripts, chart labels and the text of scrolling steps: use it when web_fetch returns little of the story, and to read what the charts label. Follow links to the story's methods or data notes when they say how a number was computed.
2. List every finding the authors draw from data: each number, comparison, ranking, share, trend or pattern the text states or a chart labels. A description of the data itself is not a finding: how many records, people, items, categories or sources it has, and how it was collected. When a chart states the same thing for each of its items (the top three for each phrase, the share for each year), that is one finding, written as one fact whose code computes it for every item at once.
3. Write each finding the files in data/ can reproduce as a fact in `facts.json`:

```json
[{"id": "women-front-shorter",
  "source": "On average, the pockets in women's jeans are 48% shorter and 6.5% narrower than men's pockets.",
  "claim": "Women's front pockets average 14.3 cm of maximum height against 23.1 cm for men.",
  "tables": {"m": "data/measurements.csv"},
  "code": "m.groupby('menWomen').maxHeightFront.mean()"}]
```

- `id`: unique in the file, a few meaningful words.
- `source`: the story's own words for this finding, quoted exactly, from its text or a chart label.
- `claim`: the finding in one sentence, with the numbers the code prints, and nothing the printout does not show: the story's own wording and numbers belong in `source`, not in the claim.
- `tables`: the files the code reads, each a variable name and the file's path from this folder, such as `data/orders.csv`; every file is read with `pd.read_csv(path)`.
- `code`: one Python expression over those variables, with `pd` (pandas) and `np` (numpy) available: the plain pandas computation whose printout shows the finding, such as a filter, a group-by, a count, a share or a sort. Do not assemble the result into a hand-made Series or dict.

Evaluate every fact from this folder the way it will be checked: read its `tables` with `pd.read_csv`, evaluate its `code`, print the value the way pandas prints it, and read the printout against the claim and the source. Every number, name and comparison in the claim must be in the printout, computed from the tables: code that writes a number itself, such as a string or a Series of typed-in values, does not count. The printout must agree with the story's numbers, up to rounding. Use the story's own definitions and filters, from its text or methods: a term means the same in every fact (if making it past the rookie contract is more than two seasons in one fact, it is more than two seasons in all of them), and a range, threshold or subset is one the story uses, never one chosen to make a number come out right. If the story's number only comes out under a definition or filter the story does not use, the finding is not reproduced. If after a fair try the data does not give the story's number (it needs other data, a different period, or the numbers differ beyond rounding), leave the finding out of facts.json.

4. Write `skipped.json`: every finding you left out, as [{"source": "the story's words", "why": "..."}].

Deliver both files, even when the data reproduces none of the story's findings: then `facts.json` is `[]`.
I'll start by exploring the data folder and reading the story.

# You Know Karen
# But do you know the names that could be “other Karens” or “future Karens?” We found them using data.
By
Jan Diehm
,
Sara Stoudt
, &
Amber Thomas
“Karen” is having a moment — and that’s not a good thing. You’ve seen her at Red Lobster , stuck in traffic with Kidz Bop , racial profiling a Filipino man chalking “Black Lives Matter” outside his home and Black women at their apartment complex pool , and with her dog off leash endangering a Black man’s life in Central Park.
But how did the name Karen become cultural flashpoint “Karen” — an entitled middle-aged White woman who needs to speak to the manager?
First, culturally: In her book, Race After Technology , scholar Ruha Benjamin explains that a name is not just a name: “Naming a child is serious business. And if you are not White in the United States, there is much more to it than personal preference.” Names can have real-world effects including influencing the chance you’ll get a callback for a job and making it impossible to submit an online college application . The “Karen” meme is exposing White women, some for the first time, to stereotyping.
Second, by popularity: According to baby name data from the Social Security Administration (which doesn’t include race/ethnicity and only categorizes by binary male/female gender), the name Karen first appeared in the female Top 20 in 1941 and spent 30 years there until it dropped out in 1971. By the 1990s, the name had fallen out of the Top 100.
Chances are you don’t know too many babies named Karen today, but when the name hit its peak at #3 in 1965, Karens were everywhere. (Important context: the US was 88.6% White at the time, so it’s safe to assume many Karens are White). It’s this swift rise and fall in popularity that’s made Karen the name so era defining and made “Karen” the meme a perfect caricature of women of a certain age and a certain privilege.
Charting the name’s popularity got us thinking: are there other names that are equally as “Karen” as Karen?
To put this question to the test, we checked baby names from the last 100 years and eliminated those that: 1) never made it into the Top 20 most popular names in any year and 2) were not present in the top list for at least 50 out of 100 years. That left us with 129 female names and 76 male names (yes, we’re going there too!). We tested each of these names, looking for the ones that most closely matched Karen’s rise and fall in popularity.
To find the closest match, we calculated the correlation between any name’s popularity over time compared to Karen’s. A correlation of 1 is a perfect match; a correlation of -1 is a name that rose and fell in popularity in the exact opposite way that Karen did (an “anti-Karen”, if you will); and the closer to 0 the correlation gets, the less that name’s popularity is like either “Karen” or “anti-Karen”. Since we’re looking for names most like Karen, we’ll focus on those that are a strong match, or anything with a correlation above 0.7. So, without further ado, introducing...
# The Other
# Karens
Female “Karens” Recently there’s been debate about whether “Karen” is a racist or sexist slur akin to using the n-word. It’s not. Need more convincing? Take it from someone named Karen herself. Need even more? Sounds like you need to check out the resources in our authors’ note . But, if you’re simply just tired of seeing the name Karen everywhere, we’ve got you covered. Here are the names to use instead for women of the same age, generation, and White privilege. (Our apologies to all the Deborahs, Debbies, and Debras.)
Show all
Male “Karens” The name Karen is largely reserved for women (especially White women) between 45–65, but is there a male equivalent? Maybe it’s Ian , like Urban Dictionary suggests. Or maybe it’s Rand of Middle Class Fancy fame. Or maybe it’s Donald, the “Karen in Chief.” Or perhaps it’s simply Greg . Nope, according to our data, it’s definitely one of the names below.
Show all
Now you know which names have the potential to become an alternative viral punchline, but what about the next generation of “Karens.” Is it really Becky ?
We’ve calculated which more recently popular names have a similar trajectory as the name Karen. These names could become “future Karens” in 10, 20, and 30 years. While these names may be “meme-able” in the coming years, people with these names don’t have to become a “Karen” themselves. But, it requires those of us with privilege to put in the work to address institutional and systemic racism, classism, and sexism. For more info, including good places to get started, please see our authors’ note .

# Authors' note
All three authors of this piece identify as White women, two of whom have names that have the potential to become “future Karens,” and one who has a name that was almost certainly a past “Karen.” We are committed to listening, learning, and being active allies in the fight for equity, inclusion, and racial and social justice. # Methodology
Baby name data for the last 100 years (1918–2018) was collected from the Social Security Administration (SSA). Race and ethnicity is not included in the original data. Baby names are classified by sex in the SSA data, but the authors would like to acknowledge that both sex and gender do not exist in a male-female binary. See more background on the baby names dataset’s limitations here .
First, for each sex we normalized each year’s name counts by the sex-specific number of babies born in total for each year. This makes sure that any underlying trends in either number of babies or number of babies of a particular sex do not get confused with a trend in name popularity.
Then we needed to see which names had a similar trajectory of popularity over time as the name Karen. There are a variety of ways to calculate a correlation between two groups. We use the Kendall rank correlation coefficient to find the other “Karens.” It measures the similarity of two sets of data based on each data point’s rank when ordered per group.
For example, take the name Karen’s popularity values, K1 and K2, for two years and another name’s popularity values, P1 and P2, for the same two years. If the rank of the values K1 and P1 are both bigger than the rank of K2 and P2 then this is evidence that the ordering of the datasets are similar, increasing the value of the correlation.
This correlation type results in high correlations between two names that have a similar shape of popularity trajectory over time rather than just focusing on their absolute popularity. That is why you see high correlations between the names Karen and Kathy despite Kathy being a less popular name than Karen, overall.
To find future “Karens,” we use the same correlation calculation, but we introduce a lag between the popularity trajectories. A handful of popularity values were dropped from the correlation computation when this lag caused us to go too far forward in time. If we shift the “Karen” trajectory forward in time and compare it to the other names’ untouched trajectories, we can see which name has a similar popularity curve that is just pushed further into the future.

## But do you know the names that could be “other Karens” or “future Karens?” We found them using data.
“Karen” is having a moment — and that’s not a good thing. You’ve seen her at [Red Lobster](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/red-lobster-karen), [stuck in traffic with Kidz Bop](https://www.washingtonpost.com/nation/2019/11/07/kidz-bop-karen-went-viral-on-camera-road-rage-lyft-passenger-she-targeted-calls-tirade-scary/), racial profiling a Filipino man [chalking “Black Lives Matter” outside his home](https://sfist.com/2020/06/14/sf-karen-filmed-confronting-pacific-heights-man-over-writing-black-lives-matter-on-his-property/) and Black women at [their apartment complex pool](https://www.theroot.com/another-day-another-karen-apartment-complex-employee-1844011486?utm_campaign=The+Root&utm_content=1591979924&utm_medium=SocialMarketing&utm_source=facebook), and [with her dog off leash endangering a Black man’s life](https://www.nytimes.com/2020/05/26/nyregion/amy-cooper-dog-central-park.html) in Central Park.
But how did the name Karen become [cultural flashpoint “Karen”](https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=Karen) — an entitled middle-aged White woman who needs to speak to the manager?
First, culturally: In her book, [Race After Technology](https://www.ruhabenjamin.com/race-after-technology), scholar Ruha Benjamin explains that a name is not just a name: “Naming a child is serious business. And if you are not White in the United States, there is much more to it than personal preference.” Names can have real-world effects including influencing the chance you’ll get a [callback for a job](https://www.nber.org/papers/w9873) and making it impossible to [submit an online college application](https://pudding.cool/2020/06/karen/). The “Karen” meme is exposing White women, some for the first time, to stereotyping.
Proportion of Babies Named Karen
Second, by popularity: According to baby name data from the [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/OACT/babynames/index.html) (which [doesn’t include](https://pudding.cool/2020/06/karen/#data-methods) race/ethnicity and only categorizes by binary male/female gender), the name Karen first appeared in the female Top 20 in 1941 and spent 30 years there until it dropped out in 1971. By the 1990s, the name had fallen out of the Top 100.
Chances are you don’t know too many babies named Karen today, but when the name hit its peak at #3 in 1965, Karens were everywhere. (Important context: the US was [88.6% White](https://www.census.gov/library/publications/1961/dec/pc-s1-10.html#:~:text=The%20white%20population%20of%20the,and%2089.3%20percent%20in%201950.) at the time, so it’s safe to assume many Karens are White). It’s this swift rise and fall in popularity that’s made Karen the name so era defining and made “Karen” [the meme](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/karen) a perfect caricature of women of a certain age and a certain privilege.
Charting the name’s popularity got us thinking: are there other names that are equally as “Karen” as Karen?
To put this question to the test, we checked baby names from the last 100 years and eliminated those that: 1) never made it into the Top 20 most popular names in any year and 2) were not present in the top list for at least 50 out of 100 years. That left us with 129 female names and 76 male names (yes, we’re going there too!). We tested each of these names, looking for the ones that most closely matched Karen’s rise and fall in popularity.
To find the closest match, we calculated the correlation between any name’s popularity over time compared to Karen’s. A correlation of 1 is a perfect match; a correlation of -1 is a name that rose and fell in popularity in the exact opposite way that Karen did (an “anti-Karen”, if you will); and the closer to 0 the correlation gets, the less that name’s popularity is like either “Karen” or “anti-Karen”. Since we’re looking for names most like Karen, we’ll focus on those that are a strong match, or anything with a correlation above 0.7. So, without further ado, introducing...

Or maybe it’s [Rand](https://www.instagram.com/p/B9sEEMOJnLC/) of Middle Class Fancy fame. Or maybe it’s Donald, the [“Karen in Chief.”](https://www.theatlantic.com/ideas/archive/2020/05/trump-social-media-scarborough/612193/) Or perhaps it’s simply [Greg](https://melmagazine.com/en-us/story/karen-has-a-husband-and-his-name-is-greg). ### Methodology
Baby name data for the last 100 years (1918–2018) was collected from the [Social Security Administration](https://www.ssa.gov/OACT/babynames/index.html) (SSA). Race and ethnicity is not included in the original data. Baby names are classified by sex in the SSA data, but the authors would like to acknowledge that both sex and gender do not exist in a male-female binary. See more background on the baby names dataset’s limitations [here](https://www.ssa.gov/OACT/babynames/background.html).
First, for each sex we normalized each year’s name counts by the sex-specific number of babies born in total for each year. This makes sure that any underlying trends in either number of babies or number of babies of a particular sex do not get confused with a trend in name popularity.
Then we needed to see which names had a similar trajectory of popularity over time as the name Karen. There are a variety of ways to calculate a correlation between two groups. We use the [Kendall rank correlation coefficient](https://towardsdatascience.com/kendall-rank-correlation-explained-dee01d99c535) to find the other “Karens.” It measures the similarity of two sets of data based on each data point’s rank when ordered per group.
For example, take the name Karen’s popularity values, K1 and K2, for two years and another name’s popularity values, P1 and P2, for the same two years. If the rank of the values K1 and P1 are both bigger than the rank of K2 and P2 then this is evidence that the ordering of the datasets are similar, increasing the value of the correlation.
This correlation type results in high correlations between two names that have a similar shape of popularity trajectory over time rather than just focusing on their absolute popularity. That is why you see high correlations between the names Karen and Kathy despite Kathy being a less popular name than Karen, overall.
To find future “Karens,” we use the same correlation calculation, but we introduce a lag between the popularity trajectories. A handful of popularity values were dropped from the correlation computation when this lag caused us to go too far forward in time. If we shift the “Karen” trajectory forward in time and compare it to the other names’ untouched trajectories, we can see which name has a similar popularity curve that is just pushed further into the future.

def walk(value, depth=1):
    yield value, depth
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        for v in value.values():

    elif isinstance(value, list):

    }


def check(data, scale: str) -> list[str]:
    """Problems a rewrite should fix; an empty list means the report is usable."""
    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        return ["顶层必须是一个 JSON 对象"]
    problems = []
    f = features(data)
    low, high = {"小": (1500, 8000), "中": (4000, 22000), "大": (10000, 60000)}[scale]
    if not low <= f["bytes"] <= high:
        problems.append(f"整份 JSON 有 {f['bytes']} 字节,这个规模应在 {low}–{high} 字节之间")
    if f["object_arrays"] == 0:
        problems.append("没有任何由对象组成的数组,数据太单薄")
    if f["numbers"] < 20:
        problems.append(f"只有 {f['numbers']} 个数值,太少")
    text = json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False)
    hits = sorted(set(m.group(0) for m in PLACEHOLDER.finditer(text)))
    if hits:
        problems.append(f"出现了占位符:{'、'.join(hits)}")
    if not re.search(r"[一-鿿]", text):
        problems.append("文本内容不是中文")
    return problems


def make_one(llm: LLM, kind: Kind, scale: str, narrative: str) -> tuple[dict | None, list[dict]]:
    messages = [{"role": "user", "content": PROMPT.format(
        name=kind.name, contents=kind.contents, scale=SCALES[scale], narrative=NARRATIVE[narrative])}]
    attempts = []
    for _ in range(MAX_REWRITES + 1):
        reply = llm.chat(messages, max_tokens=MAX_TOKENS)
        try:
            data = extract_json(reply.text)
            problems = check(data, scale)
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError) as e:
            data, problems = None, [f"不是合法的 JSON:{e}"]
        attempts.append({"problems": problems, "finish": reply.finish_reason, "seconds": reply.seconds})
        if not problems:
            return data, attempts
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply.text},
                     {"role": "user", "content": "这份数据有以下问题,请改好后重新输出完整的 JSON 代码块:\n- " + "\n- ".join(problems)}]
    return None, attempts


def split_ids(rows: list[dict], seed: int) -> dict:
    """Test kinds go to test; within every other kind, one report goes to val and the rest to train."""
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    out = {"train": [], "val": [], "test": []}
    by_kind: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_kind.setdefault(r["kind"], []).append(r["id"])
    for kind, ids in sorted(by_kind.items()):
        ids = sorted(ids)
        if next(k for k in KINDS if k.id == kind).split == "test":
            out["test"] += ids
            continue
        rng.shuffle(ids)
        out["val"].append(ids[0])
        out["train"] += ids[1:]
    return {k: sorted(v) for k, v in out.items()}


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("--per-kind", type=int, default=3)
    ap.add_argument("--kinds", help="comma-separated kind ids; default all")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    kinds = [k for k in KINDS if not args.kinds or k.id in args.kinds.split(",")]
    rng = random.Random(args.seed)
    jobs = []
    for kind in kinds:
        for i in range(args.per_kind):
            rid = f"{kind.id}-{i + 1:02d}"
            if (args.out / kind.id / f"{rid}.json").exists():
                continue
            jobs.append((kind, rid, rng.choice(list(SCALES)), rng.choice(list(NARRATIVE))))
    print(f"{len(jobs)} reports to generate with {DATA_MODEL}, {args.workers} at a time", flush=True)

    llm = LLM(model=DATA_MODEL)
    lock = threading.Lock()
    manifest = args.out / "manifest.jsonl"
    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def run(job):
        kind, rid, scale, narrative = job
        data, attempts = make_one(llm, kind, scale, narrative)
        row = {"id": rid, "kind": kind.id, "name": kind.name, "scale": scale, "narrative": narrative,
               "ok": data is not None, "attempts": attempts}
        if data is not None:
            path = args.out / kind.id / f"{rid}.json"
            path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            path.write_text(json.dumps(data, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
            row["data"] = f"{kind.id}/{rid}.json"
            row["features"] = features(data)
        with lock:
            with manifest.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        return row

    done = failed = 0
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
        for fut in as_completed([pool.submit(run, j) for j in jobs]):
            try:
                row = fut.result()
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one bad call must not stop the batch
                failed += 1
                print(f"error: {e}", flush=True)
                continue
            done += 1
            status = "ok" if row["ok"] else "FAILED " + "; ".join(row["attempts"][-1]["problems"])
            size = row.get("features", {}).get("bytes", "-")
            print(f"[{done + failed}/{len(jobs)}] {row['id']} {row['scale']} {row['narrative']} "
                  f"tries={len(row['attempts'])} bytes={size} {status}", flush=True)

    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    good = {r["id"]: r for r in rows if r["ok"]}
    split = split_ids(list(good.values()), args.seed)
    (args.out / "split.json").write_text(json.dumps(split, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"usable {len(good)}; split train {len(split['train'])} / val {len(split['val'])} / test {len(split['test'])}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    PYTHONPATH=src:../report-bench/src .venv/bin/python -m report_gepa.puddingrepo clone <cache_dir>/web <cache_dir>/repos

The source data usually sits in the story's repo under the-pudding (src/data/,

data/pudding-web has nothing for, looks for a public repo named after its slug
(also with _ for -), plus the repo OTHER names when the data sits elsewhere (the

<repos>/<slug>--<owner>-<name>/ (another); <repos>/repos.jsonl
gets one line per story with the repos found.

pack keeps the csv and tsv files outside node_modules and .git, minus the
starter template's placeholders (test.csv, sample.csv, demo folders), and the
json lists of records as csv (puddingweb.records_csv). A file
whose contents data/pudding, data/pudding-web or an earlier file already has is
dropped (the copy a build puts in docs/ or public/), and a story is kept under
the same rule as puddingweb's pack: one of its files is a table of at least
MIN_ROWS rows and MIN_COLUMNS columns. The files go to <out>/<id>/ under their own
names (with their folders when two share a name) and <out>/manifest.jsonl gets
{id, title, url, repos, published, files, bytes}. These stories are for learning
and the benchmark only: report_gepa.optimize.split does not see them.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from .optimize import DATA
from .puddingweb import KEEP, MIN_COLUMNS, MIN_ROWS, digest, manifest, records_csv, table_shape

WEB = DATA.parent / "pudding-web"
OWNER = "https://github.com/the-pudding/"
SKIP_DIRS = {".git", "node_modules", ".svelte-kit", "_records"}
OTHER = {  # story slug -> repo with its data, linked from the story page
    "love-songs": "the-pudding/pop-love-songs",
    "lenna": "the-pudding/lenna-data",
    "hamilton": "sxywu/hamilton",
    "asne": "googletrends/asne",
    "nba-moments": "googletrends/google_nba",
    "caption-contest": "nextml/caption-contest-data",
}
TEMPLATE = {"test.csv", "sample.csv", "demo-layercake.csv"}


def git(*args: str, timeout: int = 900) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout,
                          env={**os.environ, "GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE": "1"})


def clone(web: Path, repos: Path):
    repos.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    packed = {row["url"].rstrip("/").split("pudding.cool/")[-1] for row in manifest(WEB / "manifest.jsonl")}
    done = {row["url"] for row in manifest(repos / "repos.jsonl")}
    todo = [s for s in manifest(web / "summary.jsonl") if s["url"].rstrip("/") not in packed and s["url"] not in done]
    print(f"{len(todo)} stories to look up", flush=True)
    for s in todo:
        slug = s["url"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        own = next((name for name in dict.fromkeys([slug, slug.replace("-", "_")])
                    if git("ls-remote", "--heads", OWNER + name, timeout=60).returncode == 0), None)
        found = ([f"the-pudding/{own}"] if own else []) + ([OTHER[slug]] if slug in OTHER else [])
        for full in found:
            folder = repos / folder_name(slug, full)
            if not (folder / ".git").is_dir():
                # only the files pack reads: the rest of a story repo (images, audio, builds) is most of its size
                r = git("clone", "--depth", "1", "--single-branch", "--filter=blob:none", "--no-checkout",
                        f"https://github.com/{full}", str(folder))
                for step in (["sparse-checkout", "set", "--no-cone", "*.csv", "*.tsv", "*.json", "*.CSV", "*.TSV", "*.JSON"], ["checkout"]):
                    if r.returncode == 0:
                        r = git("-C", str(folder), *step)
                if r.returncode != 0:
                    print(f"{s['url']:40s} clone of {full} failed: {r.stderr.strip()[-200:]}", flush=True)
        with (repos / "repos.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"url": s["url"], "slug": slug, "title": s["title"], "repos": found}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        print(f"{s['url']:40s} {' '.join(found) or '-'}", flush=True)


def folder_name(slug: str, full: str) -> str:
    owner, name = full.split("/")
    return slug if owner == "the-pudding" and name in (slug, slug.replace("-", "_")) else f"{slug}--{owner}-{name}"


def tables(folder: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """The csv/tsv files first, then the json records, so a duplicate keeps the original csv."""
    found, records = [], []
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(folder):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS and "demo" not in d.lower())
        found += [Path(root) / f for f in sorted(files) if Path(f).suffix.lower() in KEEP and f.lower() not in TEMPLATE]
        records += [Path(root) / f for f in sorted(files) if f.endswith(".json")]
    return found + [c for p in records if (c := records_csv(p))]


def pack(repos: Path, out: Path):
    seen = {digest(p) for d in (DATA, WEB) for p in d.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in KEEP}
    taken = {row["id"] for d in (DATA, WEB) for row in manifest(d / "manifest.jsonl")}
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    rows = []
    for row in manifest(repos / "repos.jsonl"):
        folders = [repos / folder_name(row["slug"], full) for full in row["repos"]]
        fresh = []
        for p in (p for folder in folders for p in tables(folder)):
            h = digest(p)
            if h not in seen:
                seen.add(h)
                fresh.append(p)
        shapes = [table_shape(p) for p in fresh]
        if not any(r >= MIN_ROWS and c >= MIN_COLUMNS for r, c in shapes):
            print(f"{row['url']:40s} skipped: {len(fresh)} new csv/tsv files, rows x columns {shapes[:8]}", flush=True)
            continue
        sid = row["slug"] if row["slug"] not in taken else row["url"].strip("/").replace("/", "_")
        taken.add(sid)
        names = [p.name for p in fresh]
        if len(set(names)) != len(names):  # two folders hold a file of the same name
            names = [str(p.relative_to(repos)).split("/", 1)[1].replace("/", "__").replace("_records__", "") for p in fresh]
        (out / sid).mkdir()
        for p, name in zip(fresh, names):
            shutil.copy2(p, out / sid / name)
        parts = row["url"].strip("/").split("/")
        size = sum(p.stat().st_size for p in fresh)
        rows.append({"id": sid, "title": row["title"], "url": f"https://pudding.cool/{row['url'].strip('/')}/",
                     "repos": [f"https://github.com/{full}" for full in row["repos"]], "published": f"{parts[1]}/{parts[0]}" if parts[0].isdigit() else "",
                     "files": names, "bytes": size})
        print(f"{row['url']:40s} -> {sid}: {len(names)} files {size / 1e6:.2f} MB  {row['title'][:50]}", flush=True)
    (out / "manifest.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for r in rows), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(rows)} stories in {out}", flush=True)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    c = sub.add_parser("clone")
    c.add_argument("web", type=Path)
    c.add_argument("repos", type=Path)
    k = sub.add_parser("pack")
    k.add_argument("repos", type=Path)
    k.add_argument("out", type=Path)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    clone(args.web, args.repos) if args.cmd == "clone" else pack(args.repos, args.out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

facts.json is a list of facts:

    {"id": "west-returns-most",
     "claim": "Among regions with at least 100 orders, the West has the highest return rate, 19%, against 14% in the East and 13% in the North.",
     "tables": {"orders": "data/orders.csv"},
     "code": "orders[orders.region.map(orders.region.value_counts()) >= 100].groupby('region').returned.apply(lambda s: (s == 'yes').mean())"}

`tables` names the files (paths from the writer's folder, as data/orders.csv)
that are read with pd.read_csv into variables; `code` is one Python expression over them, with pd
and np available. Every fact's code is evaluated as written, in the page agent's
sandbox (report-gepa/agent/sandbox.sh: no network, nothing but the workspace),
since it is code someone else wrote, and its value is printed the way pandas
prints it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

SANDBOX = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "report-gepa" / "agent" / "sandbox.sh"
TIMEOUT = 600

RUN = r'''
import json
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

pd.set_option("display.width", 200)
out = {}
for f in json.load(open("facts.json")):
    try:
        env = {"pd": pd, "np": np}
        env.update({name: pd.read_csv(path) for name, path in f["tables"].items()})
        value = eval(f["code"], env)
        out[f["id"]] = {"output": value.to_string() if hasattr(value, "to_string") else str(value)}
    except Exception as e:
        out[f["id"]] = {"error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"[:300]}
print(json.dumps(out))
'''


class FactError(ValueError):
    """facts.json that cannot be read as a list of facts."""


def load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    try:
        facts = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        raise FactError(f"{path.name}: {e}") from e
    keys = ("id", "claim", "tables", "code")
    if not isinstance(facts, list) or not all(isinstance(f, dict) and all(f.get(k) for k in keys) for f in facts):
        raise FactError(f"{path.name}: not a list of facts with {', '.join(keys)}")
    return facts


def run(facts: list[dict], data: list[Path]) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """Every fact's printed value ("output") or why it failed ("error"), by id.
    `data` is what the writer found in data/: files and folders, by their own names."""
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        ws = Path(tmp)
        (ws / "data").mkdir()
        for p in data:
            if p.is_dir():
                shutil.copytree(p, ws / "data" / p.name, copy_function=os.link)
            else:
                os.link(p, ws / "data" / p.name)
        (ws / "facts.json").write_text(json.dumps(facts), encoding="utf-8")
        (ws / "run.py").write_text(RUN, encoding="utf-8")
        proc = subprocess.run([str(SANDBOX), str(ws), "python3 run.py"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=TIMEOUT)
    if proc.returncode != 0:
        return {f["id"]: {"error": f"the run failed: {proc.stderr.strip()[-300:]}"} for f in facts}
    return json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])

"""The score of a page: the one definition the benchmark, GEPA and TF-GRPO share.

    PYTHONPATH=../report-gepa/src:src ../report-gepa/.venv/bin/python -m report_bench.score submissions/<system> [--tasks a,b] [--out runs/<system>] [--workers 4] [--browsers 2] | tee runs/<system>.log

score_page scores one delivered page (a folder with index.html and facts.json,
see TASK.md) made from `data`, the files and folders its writer found in data/:

1. capture: the page is captured with the data (capture.py) into <out>/evidence.
2. trust (1.x, trust.py): renders, refs hold, data accurate. Any violated item
   makes the score 0 and the page is not judged further: a page that misstates
   its data is not a better page for being clear or pretty.
3. expression (2.x) and aesthetics (3.x): 2.2 argument and 2.3 narrative from
   the page's prose, one call each (article.py); the rest from the screenshots,
   one judge call per dimension (judge.py).
4. the score: the mean of the scored items, equal weights until weights are
   fitted on whole-page labels, except that 2.2 and 2.3 count as one item
   between them (WEIGHT): together they say how the article is told.

A check that gives no usable answer (1.3 without parseable JSON, a judge call
that leaves an item without a score) is asked again, up to TRIES times in all;
the tries are kept, so a restart does not ask a hopeless page again. A page whose
checks are still missing an answer is `complete: false`: its score covers only
what was answered, and callers that compare pages (TF-GRPO) leave it out.

Everything is kept in <out>: evidence/, trust.json, judgements.json,
article.json and result.json, and reused when present, so a restart or a repeated request costs
nothing. The result's feedback lines (every trust problem, every item's score and
reason, the page's scroll facts) are what GEPA reflects on.

The benchmark command scores submissions/<system>/<id>/ for every task in
out/tasks/ with the task's data, writes <out>/scores.jsonl and prints the means by
source. A task with no page scores 0.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor, as_completed
from contextlib import nullcontext
from pathlib import Path
from statistics import mean

from . import article as A
from . import judge as J
from . import trust as T
from .capture import capture
from .llm import OutOfCredit
from .rubric import load

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
TASKS = ROOT / "out" / "tasks"
MODEL = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"  # GEPA's and TF-GRPO's judge, so benchmark scores compare with their runs
TRIES = 3
WEIGHT = {"2.2": 0.5, "2.3": 0.5}  # argument and narrative are halves of one item; every other item weighs 1


def _read(path: Path, default):
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if path.exists() else default


def _write(path: Path, value) -> None:
    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")


def _trust(page: Path, ev: Path, out: Path, model: str) -> dict:
    path = out / "trust.json"
    record = _read(path, None)
    tries = record["tries"] if record else 0
    while tries < TRIES and (record is None or record["items"].get("1.3", {}).get("violated", False) is None):
        tries += 1
        record = {**T.trust(ev, page / "facts.json", model), "tries": tries}
        if "1.3" in record["items"]:
            (out / "trust-prompt.txt").write_text(record["items"]["1.3"].pop("prompt"), encoding="utf-8")
        _write(path, record)
    return record


def _judge(ev: Path, out: Path, model: str) -> dict:
    path = out / "judgements.json"
    items = _read(path, {})
    tries = items.setdefault("tries", {})
    scored = [it for it in load().values() if it.scored and not it.prose_only]
    for dim in ([it for it in scored if it.id.startswith(d)] for d in ("2.", "3.")):
        name = dim[0].id[0] + ".x"
        while tries.get(name, 0) < TRIES and not all(items.get(it.id, {}).get("score") is not None for it in dim):
            tries[name] = tries.get(name, 0) + 1
            try:
                items.update(J.page_group(dim, ev, model)[1])
            except OutOfCredit:
                raise
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - asked again; still missing, the page is incomplete
                print(f"[judge] {out.name} {name}: FAILED {str(e)[:200]}", flush=True)
            _write(path, items)
    return items


def _article(ev: Path, out: Path, model: str) -> dict:
    path = out / "article.json"
    items = _read(path, {})
    tries = items.setdefault("tries", {})
    for it in (it for it in load().values() if it.prose_only):
        while tries.get(it.id, 0) < TRIES and items.get(it.id, {}).get("score") is None:
            tries[it.id] = tries.get(it.id, 0) + 1
            try:
                items[it.id] = A.judge(it.id, ev, model)
            except OutOfCredit:
                raise
            except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - asked again; still missing, the page is incomplete
                print(f"[article] {out.name} {it.id}: FAILED {str(e)[:200]}", flush=True)
            _write(path, items)
    return items


def score_page(page: Path, data: list[Path], out: Path, model: str = MODEL, browsers: threading.Semaphore | None = None) -> dict:
    """Score the page in `page` (index.html, facts.json) made from `data`; see the module text."""
    path = out / "result.json"
    if path.exists():
        return _read(path, None)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ev = out / "evidence"
    if not (ev / "evidence.json").exists():
        with browsers or nullcontext():
            capture(str((page / "index.html").resolve()), ev, None, data)
    trust = _trust(page, ev, out, model)
    feedback = T.feedback(trust)
    rubric = {it.id: it for it in load().values() if it.scored}
    if trust["vetoed"]:
        result = {"score": 0.0, "vetoed": trust["vetoed"], "parts": {}, "complete": True,
                  "summary": "vetoed by " + ",".join(trust["vetoed"])}
    else:
        items = {**_judge(ev, out, model), **_article(ev, out, model)}
        parts = {k: items[k]["score"] for k in rubric if items.get(k, {}).get("score") is not None}
        for k, it in rubric.items():
            if k in parts:
                r = items[k]
                feedback.append(f"{k} {it.name}:{parts[k]:.2f}。{r.get('where') or ''} {r.get('reason') or ''}".strip())
        missing = [k for k in rubric if k not in parts]
        unchecked = trust["items"].get("1.3", {}).get("violated") is None
        weights = {k: WEIGHT.get(k, 1.0) for k in parts}
        result = {"score": sum(v * weights[k] for k, v in parts.items()) / sum(weights.values()) if parts else 0.0,
                  "vetoed": [], "parts": parts,
                  "complete": not missing and not unchecked,
                  "summary": " ".join(f"{k}={v:.2f}" for k, v in parts.items())
                             + (f"  unjudged {','.join(missing)}" if missing else "") + ("  1.3 unchecked" if unchecked else "")}
    e = _read(ev / "evidence.json", {})
    feedback.append(f"页面高 {e.get('page_height')}px,滚动截了 {len(e.get('frames', []))} 帧,"
                    f"滚动时固定在屏幕上的图 {sum(1 for c in e.get('scroll_story', []) if c['pinned'])} 张。")
    result["feedback"] = feedback
    _write(path, result)
    return result


def task_data(task: str) -> list[Path]:
    """A benchmark task's files, as a submission's writer finds them in data/."""
    return sorted((TASKS / task / "data").iterdir())


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("system", type=Path, help="submissions/<system>: one <id>/ with index.html and facts.json per task")
    ap.add_argument("--tasks", help="comma-separated task ids (default: all)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=Path, help="default runs/<system>")
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    ap.add_argument("--browsers", type=int, default=2)
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    listed = {json.loads(l)["id"]: json.loads(l)["source"] for l in (ROOT / "out" / "tasks.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()}
    tasks = args.tasks.split(",") if args.tasks else list(listed)
    out = args.out or ROOT / "runs" / args.system.name
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    browsers = threading.Semaphore(args.browsers)
    print(f"== {args.system.name}: {len(tasks)} tasks, judge {args.model}, out {out}", flush=True)

    def one(task: str) -> dict:
        if not (args.system / task / "index.html").exists():
            return {"score": 0.0, "summary": "no page"}
        return score_page(args.system / task, task_data(task), out / task, args.model, browsers)

    results = {}
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
        jobs = {pool.submit(one, t): t for t in tasks}
        for f in as_completed(jobs):
            r = f.result()
            results[jobs[f]] = r
            print(f"{jobs[f]:24} {r['score']:.3f}  {r['summary'][:160]}", flush=True)
    (out / "scores.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps({"task": t, "source": listed[t], **{k: v for k, v in results[t].items() if k != "feedback"}},
                                                         ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for t in tasks), encoding="utf-8")
    for source in dict.fromkeys(listed[t] for t in tasks):
        s = [results[t]["score"] for t in tasks if listed[t] == source]
        print(f"{source:13} {len(s):4d} tasks  mean {mean(s):.3f}", flush=True)
    print(f"{'all':13} {len(tasks):4d} tasks  mean {mean(results[t]['score'] for t in tasks):.3f}", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Write down a Pudding story's findings, as facts, with a pi agent that reads the story on the web.

    PYTHONPATH=src:../report-bench/src .venv/bin/python -m report_gepa.originals <out_dir> [id ...] [--workers 8] [--model m]

These are the answers for rubric 2.1 (finding coverage): the findings the
original's authors drew from the task's data, written the way a page's
facts.json is (report-bench/TASK.md), so a page's facts can be matched against
them. Without ids, every task with an original.json in report-bench/out/answers.

The agent (agent/gen.mjs with WEB_TOOLS=1) gets the task's data under data/ and
the story's address. It reads the story with web_fetch and web_view (agent/web.mjs,
run outside the sandbox), lists every finding the authors state or label, and
writes the ones the data reproduces as facts, each quoting the story's words in
`source`; the rest go to skipped.json with the reason. Then every fact is run
again and its claim read against its printout, as trust.py does for a page (1.2,
1.3), and its source looked up in the text the agent's web tools returned. The
facts that pass are the answer, answer.json; the others are listed in
record.json under `dropped`. Each task lives in <out_dir>/<id>/: facts.json (the
agent's), answer.json, skipped.json, record.json and session.jsonl; the copied
data is removed afterwards. A task whose answer.json exists is skipped, so a
stopped run picks up where it was. With --answers, answer.json is also copied to
report-bench/out/answers/<id>/facts.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import html
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

from report_bench.llm import OutOfCredit, credit_refused
from report_bench.trust import claims_hold, run_facts

from .generate import GEN_MODEL, ROOT, run_agent

BENCH = ROOT.parent / "report-bench" / "out"

SYSTEM = """You are a careful data analyst. You read a published data story and write down, as checkable facts, the findings its authors drew from their data. You quote the story exactly, you compute every number from the files you are given, and you never type a number into code. You work in English."""

TASK = """The folder `data/` holds the data behind a published data story, "{title}": {url}
The files: {files}

Write down the story's findings that this data reproduces.

1. Read the story on the web. web_fetch returns the page as the server sends it. web_view opens it in a browser and scrolls it like a reader, so it also gets text drawn by scripts, chart labels and the text of scrolling steps: use it when web_fetch returns little of the story, and to read what the charts label. Follow links to the story's methods or data notes when they say how a number was computed.
2. List every finding the authors draw from data: each number, comparison, ranking, share, trend or pattern the text states or a chart labels. A description of the data itself is not a finding: how many records, people, items, categories or sources it has, and how it was collected. When a chart states the same thing for each of its items (the top three for each phrase, the share for each year), that is one finding, written as one fact whose code computes it for every item at once.
3. Write each finding the files in data/ can reproduce as a fact in `facts.json`:

```json
[{{"id": "women-front-shorter",
  "source": "On average, the pockets in women's jeans are 48% shorter and 6.5% narrower than men's pockets.",
  "claim": "Women's front pockets average 14.3 cm of maximum height against 23.1 cm for men.",
  "tables": {{"m": "data/measurements.csv"}},
  "code": "m.groupby('menWomen').maxHeightFront.mean()"}}]
```

- `id`: unique in the file, a few meaningful words.
- `source`: the story's own words for this finding, quoted exactly, from its text or a chart label.
- `claim`: the finding in one sentence, with the numbers the code prints, and nothing the printout does not show: the story's own wording and numbers belong in `source`, not in the claim.
- `tables`: the files the code reads, each a variable name and the file's path from this folder, such as `data/orders.csv`; every file is read with `pd.read_csv(path)`.
- `code`: one Python expression over those variables, with `pd` (pandas) and `np` (numpy) available: the plain pandas computation whose printout shows the finding, such as a filter, a group-by, a count, a share or a sort. Do not assemble the result into a hand-made Series or dict.

Evaluate every fact from this folder the way it will be checked: read its `tables` with `pd.read_csv`, evaluate its `code`, print the value the way pandas prints it, and read the printout against the claim and the source. Every number, name and comparison in the claim must be in the printout, computed from the tables: code that writes a number itself, such as a string or a Series of typed-in values, does not count. The printout must agree with the story's numbers, up to rounding. Use the story's own definitions and filters, from its text or methods: a term means the same in every fact (if making it past the rookie contract is more than two seasons in one fact, it is more than two seasons in all of them), and a range, threshold or subset is one the story uses, never one chosen to make a number come out right. If the story's number only comes out under a definition or filter the story does not use, the finding is not reproduced. If after a fair try the data does not give the story's number (it needs other data, a different period, or the numbers differ beyond rounding), leave the finding out of facts.json.

4. Write `skipped.json`: every finding you left out, as [{{"source": "the story's words", "why": "..."}}].

Deliver both files, even when the data reproduces none of the story's findings: then `facts.json` is `[]`.
"""


def task_text(task_id: str) -> str:
    original = json.loads((BENCH / "answers" / task_id / "original.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    task = json.loads((BENCH / "tasks" / task_id / "task.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return TASK.format(title=original["title"], url=original["url"], files=", ".join(task["files"]))


def _norm(s: str) -> str:
    # web_fetch leaves entities such as ‘ undecoded, so both sides are unescaped first
    return re.sub(r"[\W_]+", " ", html.unescape(s)).lower().strip()


def quoted(source: str, read: str) -> bool:
    """Whether every part of a quote is in what was read; parts joined by an ellipsis may sit apart, as chart labels do."""
    parts = [_norm(x) for x in re.split(r"\.\.\.|\u2026", source)]
    return bool(any(parts)) and all(x in read for x in parts if x)


def read_on_web(session: Path) -> str:
    """Everything the agent's web tools returned, normalised for looking quotes up."""
    text = []
    for line in session.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        try:
            m = json.loads(line).get("message", {})
        except json.JSONDecodeError:  # a line cut off while the file was written
            continue
        if m.get("role") == "toolResult" and m.get("toolName") in ("web_fetch", "web_view"):
            text += [c.get("text", "") for c in m.get("content", []) if c.get("type") == "text"]
    return _norm(" ".join(text))


def extract(task_id: str, out_dir: Path, model: str, effort: str = "high") -> dict:
    ws = out_dir / task_id
    shutil.rmtree(ws, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.copytree(BENCH / "tasks" / task_id / "data", ws / "data")
    task_path = out_dir / f"{task_id}.task.md"
    task_path.write_text(task_text(task_id), encoding="utf-8")
    system_path = out_dir / "system.md"
    run = run_agent(ws, system_path, model, effort, f"  {task_id}", task_path, output="facts.json")
    if credit_refused(run.get("error")):
        shutil.rmtree(ws, ignore_errors=True)
        raise OutOfCredit(run["error"])
    record = {"id": task_id, "model": model, "effort": effort, "run": run}
    data = sorted((ws / "data").iterdir())
    problems, facts, results = run_facts(ws / "facts.json", data)
    record["facts"] = len(facts)
    record["problems"] = problems
    if not facts and not problems:  # the story states nothing this data reproduces
        record["dropped"], record["answer"] = [], 0
        (ws / "answer.json").write_text("[]", encoding="utf-8")
    if facts and not problems:
        check = claims_hold(facts, results, model)
        record["wrong"] = check["wrong"]
        record["verdicts"] = check["verdicts"]
        if check["wrong"] is not None:
            read = read_on_web(ws / "session.jsonl") if (ws / "session.jsonl").exists() else ""
            wrong = {v["id"] for v in check["wrong"]}
            dropped = [{"id": f["id"], "why": "claim does not agree with its printout"} for f in facts if f["id"] in wrong]
            dropped += [{"id": f["id"], "why": "source not in the story as read"} for f in facts
                        if f["id"] not in wrong and not quoted(str(f.get("source", "")), read)]
            gone = {d["id"] for d in dropped}
            answer = [f for f in facts if f["id"] not in gone]
            record["dropped"] = dropped
            record["answer"] = len(answer)
            (ws / "answer.json").write_text(json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    skipped = ws / "skipped.json"
    try:
        record["skipped"] = len(json.loads(skipped.read_text(encoding="utf-8")))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
        record["skipped"] = None
    shutil.rmtree(ws / "data")
    (ws / "record.json").write_text(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1), encoding="utf-8")
    return record


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("out", type=Path)
    ap.add_argument("ids", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--model", default=GEN_MODEL)
    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=8)
    ap.add_argument("--answers", action="store_true", help="copy each answer.json to report-bench/out/answers/<id>/facts.json")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    ids = args.ids or sorted(p.parent.name for p in (BENCH / "answers").glob("*/original.json"))
    args.out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (args.out / "system.md").write_text(SYSTEM, encoding="utf-8")
    os.environ["WEB_TOOLS"] = "1"  # run_agent passes the environment on to gen.mjs

    def one(task_id):
        if (args.out / task_id / "answer.json").exists():  # done in an earlier run
            return
        try:
            r = extract(task_id, args.out, args.model)
        except OutOfCredit:
            raise
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - one task's failure is reported, not the end of the run
            print(f"{task_id}: crashed {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}", flush=True)
            return
        answer = args.out / task_id / "answer.json"
        if args.answers and answer.exists():
            shutil.copy2(answer, BENCH / "answers" / task_id / "facts.json")
        print(f"{task_id}: facts={r['facts']} answer={r.get('answer')} dropped={len(r.get('dropped', []))} "
              f"skipped={r['skipped']} problems={len(r['problems'])} {r['run'].get('seconds')}s steps={r['run'].get('steps')}",
              flush=True)

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.workers) as pool:
        list(pool.map(one, ids))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Pudding stories whose data is there but not as a table: one recipe each makes it one.

    PYTHONPATH=src:../report-bench/src .venv/bin/python -m report_gepa.puddingmerge <cache_dir> data/pudding-merge [--stories a,b]

The other sources left these out because the data is spread over many small
files (one per game, station, contest, person or name), is json that is not a
list of records, or sits on a host other than pudding.cool. Each recipe in
RECIPES fetches the files (repos shallow-cloned into <cache_dir>, only the paths
it reads) and writes tables to <out>/<id>/:

    concat  many files of one shape -> one table; the column a file stood for
            (station, contest, ...) comes from its name
    json    nested json -> long rows (name, spelling, count), map properties ->
            a row per region, records -> a row per record
    copy    a file the page loads from another host

<out>/manifest.jsonl gets {id, title, url, published, files, bytes}. A story the
benchmark already has (report-bench/tasks.json) is refused.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError

from .optimize import DATA
from .puddingweb import STORY_LIST, manifest

BENCH = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "report-bench" / "tasks.json"

csv.field_size_limit(sys.maxsize)


def checkout(repo: str, paths: list[str], cache: Path) -> Path:
    """Shallow clone with only `paths` (gitignore-style patterns) checked out; reused if present."""
    dst = cache / repo.replace("/", "__")
    env = {**os.environ, "GIT_LFS_SKIP_SMUDGE": "1"}
    if not (dst / ".git").exists():
        subprocess.run(["git", "clone", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", "--no-checkout", "--quiet",
                        f"https://github.com/{repo}", str(dst)], check=True, env=env)
    subprocess.run(["git", "sparse-checkout", "set", "--no-cone", *paths], cwd=dst, check=True, env=env)
    subprocess.run(["git", "checkout", "--quiet"], cwd=dst, check=True, env=env)
    return dst


def get(url: str) -> bytes | None:
    """The file at url, None when there is none (404); a dropped connection is tried again, up to 4 times."""
    for wait in (2, 4, 8, 16, None):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as r:
                return r.read()
        except HTTPError as e:
            if e.code == 404:
                return None

def concat(parts: list[tuple[dict, Path]], dst: Path) -> int:
    """Write the rows of every file to dst, each with its own extra columns in front; return the row count."""
    header = list(dict.fromkeys(k for extra, _ in parts for k in extra))
    for _, p in parts:
        with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
            header += [k for k in next(csv.reader(f)) if k not in header]
    n = 0
    with dst.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as g:
        w = csv.DictWriter(g, header)
        w.writeheader()
        for extra, p in parts:
            with p.open(encoding="utf-8-sig", newline="") as f:
                for row in csv.DictReader(f):
                    w.writerow({**row, **extra})
                    n += 1
    return n


def write(dst: Path, header: list[str], rows) -> int:
    n = 0
    with dst.open("w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as g:
        w = csv.writer(g)
        w.writerow(header)
        for r in rows:
            w.writerow(r)

def pack(src: Path, out: Path):
    seen = {digest(p) for p in DATA.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.suffix.lower() in KEEP}
    taken = {row["id"] for row in manifest(DATA / "manifest.jsonl")}
    shutil.rmtree(out, ignore_errors=True)
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    rows = []
    for row in manifest(src / "summary.jsonl"):
        folder = src / row["slug"]
        files = sorted(p for p in folder.glob("*") if p.suffix.lower() in KEEP) if folder.is_dir() else []
        files += [c for p in sorted(folder.glob("*.json")) if (c := records_csv(p))] if folder.is_dir() else []
        fresh = []
        for p in files:
            h = digest(p)
            if h not in seen:
                seen.add(h)
                fresh.append(p)
        size = sum(p.stat().st_size for p in fresh)
        shapes = [table_shape(p) for p in fresh]
        if not any(r >= MIN_ROWS and c >= MIN_COLUMNS for r, c in shapes):
            print(f"{row['url']:40s} skipped: {len(fresh)} new csv/tsv files, rows x columns {shapes}", flush=True)
            continue
        sid = row["url"].rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        sid = sid if sid not in taken else row["slug"]
        taken.add(sid)
        names = [p.name.split("__")[-1] for p in fresh]
        names = names if len(set(names)) == len(names) else [p.name for p in fresh]  # the short names collide
        (out / sid).mkdir()
        for p, name in zip(fresh, names):
            shutil.copy2(p, out / sid / name)
        parts = row["url"].strip("/").split("/")
        published = f"{parts[1]}/{parts[0]}" if parts[0].isdigit() else ""
        rows.append({"id": sid, "title": row["title"], "url": f"https://pudding.cool/{row['url'].strip('/')}/",
                     "published": published, "files": names, "bytes": size})
        print(f"{row['url']:40s} -> {sid}: {len(names)} files {size / 1e6:.2f} MB  {row['title'][:50]}", flush=True)
    (out / "manifest.jsonl").write_text("".join(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n" for r in rows), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(rows)} stories in {out}", flush=True)
